Implement GitHub issue #57, "R1 06b: Move the app entry to Foldkit", in chrisdoc/surveybeat-next. This is production code. You're in your own git worktree. Run `git fetch origin` and create branch `t3/r1-06b-foldkit` from origin/main. Main holds slices 01–06 and 14: the Alchemy stack with `pr-<n>` stages, AuthKit sign-in, People/Teams/settings, the Pulse editor, email, and the privacy suite. The web app in `apps/web` currently uses React, Tailwind v4, and Base UI, with a hash router.

## Read first
- `gh issue view 57`: the acceptance criteria. They're binding.
- Foldkit's docs: https://foldkit.dev/ , /get-started, /core/architecture, /core/routing-and-navigation, /core/server-rendering, /ui/overview, /testing, /react/coming-from-react. Read them with your web fetch tool. Foldkit is pre-1.0 (about v0.170) and requires Effect ~4.1.0; we pin effect 4.1.2. Use the real API from the installed packages' .d.ts files, not guesses.
- docs/adr/0007, docs/adr/0008, GLOSSARY.md. The existing `apps/web/src` (App.tsx, Directory.tsx, the pulse screens, session.ts, directory.ts, messages/catalog.ts). `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`. The e2e in `infra/tests/e2e`.
- The answer-page measurement method: on branch `prototype/answer-page`, see `git show prototype/answer-page:prototype/answer-page/RESULTS.md` and its `scripts/`.

## Scope (summary; #57 is binding)
- Pin `foldkit`, `@foldkit/ui`, `@foldkit/vite-plugin` exactly in the catalog. Respect pnpm minimumReleaseAge. NEVER add minimumReleaseAgeExclude; if the newest version is too fresh, use the previous one.
- Rewrite every existing app screen in the Elm architecture (Model as an Effect Schema, Messages, update, Commands, view), with Foldkit's typed routing replacing the hash router:
  - sign-in states;
  - Create an Organization, not part of an Organization, and the Organization picker;
  - Teams list, Team detail, and Organization settings;
  - Pulse list and Pulse editor.

  Keep the same API calls, behaviour, and message catalog keys. Accessible components come from `@foldkit/ui`.
- Remove React, react-dom, and @base-ui/react from apps/web. React stays only in `packages/emails`. Tailwind v4 and the tokens stay.
- Adapt the oxlint rules:
  - `no-literal-ui-text` moves from JSX to Foldkit `h()` view calls, with fixtures proving it fails on literal text;
  - `domain-boundary` additionally bans `foldkit` in `packages/domain`, `packages/api`, and the answer entry.
- Tests: Foldkit story tests and scene tests for each screen's main flows, in Vitest. The e2e must keep passing on the PR stage.
- Answer-page check: build the answer page's first screen with Foldkit static prerendering plus hydration in a scratch dir (NOT in apps/web) and measure it with the prototype's Lighthouse method: critical JS gzip, FCP, LCP. Report the numbers. The decision rule: only if critical JS ≤ 10 KB gzip AND LCP ≤ 1.3 s could the answer page switch later. Don't switch it in this PR.
- Amend ADR 0008: Foldkit replaces React and Base UI for the app, the answer-page result goes in, and Foldkit's pre-1.0 status is listed as an accepted risk.
- No `any`, and no `as` outside tests.

## Validation
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `typecheck`, `typecheck:effect`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `test:privacy`, and the web build all pass.

Replace React and Base UI in `apps/web`'s **app entry** with Foldkit and `@foldkit/ui`, before more UI slices land.

## Acceptance criteria
- `foldkit`, `@foldkit/ui`, and `@foldkit/vite-plugin` are pinned exactly in the catalog (pre-1.0; they move together with the Effect pins). Respect pnpm's minimumReleaseAge, and never add minimumReleaseAgeExclude. Foldkit requires Effect ~4.1.0, which matches our 4.1.2.

  - Create an Organization, Not part of an Organization, and the Organization picker;
  - the Teams list, Team detail, and Organization settings;
  - the Pulse list and the Pulse editor (from slice 06).
- React, react-dom, and `@base-ui/react` are removed from `apps/web`'s app entry. React stays ONLY in `packages/emails` (React Email renders on the server).
- Tailwind v4 stays. The design tokens stay as CSS custom properties.
- The oxlint rule `surveybeat/no-literal-ui-text` is adapted from JSX to Foldkit's `h()` view calls, with fixtures proving it still fails on literal text. The `domain-boundary` rule bans `foldkit` imports in `domain`, `api`, and the answer entry (unless the answer-page check below passes).

If critical JS stays ≤ 10 KB gzip and LCP ≤ 1.3 s, record that so a later slice can switch. Otherwise the answer page stays plain TS. Either way, write the numbers in the PR.
- ADR 0008 is amended to say Foldkit replaces React and Base UI for the app, records the answer-page result, and lists Foldkit's pre-1.0 status as an accepted risk.

## Follows
ADR 0007, 0008. See also the scope decisions on the map (#2) and the existing screens from #37, #38, #40.

# SurveyBeat

Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Two Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`) and the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`).

Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, WorkOS sign-in, email, and observability.

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the React app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*` or Alchemy, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, and `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST` in the environment.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

# A one-tap rating link only preselects; the answer is saved when the member confirms it

SPEC §5.1 said each rating link in an email "records the answer". Email security scanners (Microsoft Defender runs headless Chrome) fetch every link, so recording on GET would count scanners as voters. Some scanners can also produce trusted events, so saving on any interaction would still be unsafe. A rating link (`/a#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`) therefore opens the answer page with that value preselected and writes nothing. The answer is saved only when the member taps "Save and continue", which sits directly under the anonymity statement, or changes the value. A member who taps in the email and leaves without touching the page loses that answer. We accept that loss as the price of never counting a scanner.

## Consequences

- The token exchange that loads the page has no side effects, so R1 has no open tracking at all.
- The anonymity statement is always read before the first Answer is stored.
- One-tap needs a rating Question first in the Pulse. Otherwise the email offers only "Open check-in".

# Agent Development Notes

Preferences and conventions for coding agents working on this repository. This file is the always-on summary. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it, so every tool that reads either name gets the same rules.

## Pull request attribution

Never put AI attribution in a pull request title or description, regardless of which agent creates or updates it. Requirements to attribute agent-posted comments, reviews, or messages on external services still apply to pull request comments and reviews, but **not** to the pull request title or description. Those fields become commit metadata on squash merge. Do not add an attribution footer even if a template, tool, or other instruction asks for one. After creating or updating a pull request, read its title and description back and remove any AI attribution added by tooling or the service.

Depth lives in these places:

- Website docs at `packages/website/src/page/` (Mount, Command, Subscription, Submodels, OutMessage, best practices).
- The exemplar files below.
- The repo-local skills in `skills/`. These target consumer Foldkit apps, not work on this repository. Read them for framework semantics, not as always-on repo-maintenance guidance.
- `.agents/writing-prose.md`, worked examples for the prose rules below.

Read those when a rule needs context.

## Project Conventions

- "Foldkit" is always capitalized in prose. The only exception is the npm package name (`foldkit`) and import paths.
- Evaluate work at framework scale. In-repo consumer count is evidence, not a value heuristic. Foldkit may have only one or two internal consumers for an API, tool, documentation primitive, or shared abstraction that many downstream applications will need. Consider the external consumer base, public surface longevity, consistency costs, and the repository's role as an exemplar before deciding that a change is too narrow. Still require a concrete framework-level use case; do not invoke hypothetical consumers to justify speculative complexity.
- In prose, capitalize architecture types: Model, Message, Command, Subscription, Mount, ManagedResource, CustomElement, Submodel, OutMessage. Keep lowercase for plain functions: view, update, init.
- Always use Schema types (not plain TypeScript types), full names like `Message` (not `Msg`), and `withReturnType` (not `as const` or type casting).
- Foldkit is tightly coupled to Effect-TS. Do not suggest solutions outside the Effect ecosystem. Check existing features in `create-foldkit-app` before suggesting new ones.
- Push back on any direction that violates Elm Architecture principles: unidirectional data flow, Messages as facts, Model as single source of truth, side effects confined to Commands. Flag the issue and propose the Foldkit approach that preserves those principles.
- Run TypeScript scripts with `node` directly, as in `node scripts/check-peer-floors.ts`. Every Node version in `engines` strips types, so the workspace has no `tsx`, `vite-node`, or other loader, and none may be added. Node resolves imports literally: write the extension the file has, and reach package code through its built entry rather than its source. A script whose module graph needs Vite's resolution, such as the website's `openapi` and `prerender`, is bundled with `vite build --ssr` first and the bundle runs under `node`. `erasableSyntaxOnly` in the base tsconfig keeps every source within what Node can strip.

## Cloudflare Workers Guide

The [Foldkit framework guide for Cloudflare Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/foldkit/) lives in `cloudflare/cloudflare-docs` at `src/content/docs/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/foldkit.mdx`. Review and update it when changes to `create-foldkit-app`, Node.js requirements, SPA/SSG/SSR build outputs, the Worker `fetch` entry point, or Wrangler configuration affect its instructions.

## Exemplar Files

Read these before writing code. They calibrate the quality bar.

- Library internals (`packages/foldkit/src/`): `runtime/runtime.ts`, `route/parser.ts`.
- Application architecture (`packages/website/`, examples, apps built with Foldkit): `packages/typing-game/client/src/` for Submodels, OutMessage, update/Message patterns, view decomposition.

The principles below apply broadly. Calibrate to the right context: library design when inside `packages/foldkit/src/`, application architecture elsewhere.

## Naming

- Messages are verb-first, past-tense facts: `SubmittedUsernameForm`, `CreatedRoom`, `PressedKey`. Verb prefixes: `Clicked*`, `Updated*`, `Succeeded*`/`Failed*` (when failure is meaningful), `Completed*` (every other Command result), `Got*` (child Submodel results only).
- Never name a Message `NoOp`. This is a rule about the name, not about the behavior: a Message whose update handler changes nothing is fine and often necessary, and it gets a descriptive name stating the fact like any other. For example: `IgnoredMouseClick`, `SuppressedSpaceScroll`. Dispatch the Message even when update leaves the Model unchanged. `Completed*` mirrors the Command name verb-first: `LockScroll` produces `CompletedLockScroll`.
- A Command's result Message is named from the Command, not from the fact it reports, and that holds whether or not it carries a payload: `DetermineStartTime` produces `CompletedDetermineStartTime`, never `DeterminedStartTime`. A Message with more than one cause is named for the fact, such as `EndedAnimation`, which both `WaitForAnimationSettled` and each component's `DetectMovementOrAnimationEnd` race produce. When a generic factory returns an instance-owned Command and Message namespace, name the result Message from the Command member rather than its generated runtime name. An instance suffix used only to distinguish runtime Command identities does not join the Message tag: `postsQuery.Fetch` has the runtime name `FetchPosts` and produces `postsQuery.Message.CompletedFetch`.
- Commands are verb-first imperatives: `FetchWeather`, `FocusButton`, `LockScroll`. Name the effect the Command's execute body performs, not the later Model transition caused when update handles its result. A timer that only waits before update starts a dismissal is `WaitBeforeDismissal`, not `DismissAfter`.
- Mount Definitions are verb-first imperatives like Commands: `AnchorPopover`, `PortalPopoverBackdrop`, `SyncSidebarScroll`. Result Messages follow the standard Message convention.
- Use names that are immediately understandable in context. Avoid opaque abbreviations and unexplained single-letter names: `callbacks`, not `cbs`; `context`, not `c`; `(tickCount)`, not `(t)`. Conventional technical shorthand is allowed when it is the normal spelling for the domain, including `attrs`, `props`, `args`, `dir`, `ctx`, `fn`, `DOM`, `URL`, and `VNode`. Established API and DSL bindings such as `h` are also allowed, as is `ih` for `inertHtml`, which reads as the inert counterpart to `h` and keeps the two builders distinguishable at every call site. Conventional single-letter Effect type parameters such as `A`, `E`, and `R` are allowed when they stand alone. When several parameters have the same role, spell out each complete semantic name and name it for its actual source, such as `ChildRequirements` and `OutMessageStepRequirements`, not `ChildR` and `ParentR`. Prefer a more precise semantic name when one exists, such as `toMessage` instead of `f`.
- Don't suffix Command variables with `Command`. The type already says so.
- Prefix `Option`-typed values with `maybe`. Never prefix `T | undefined` values with `nullable`; name them plainly and let the type carry the optionality.
- Prefix booleans with `is`.
- Name functions by their precise effect: `enqueueMessage`, not `addMessage`. A reader should never need to check a type signature to understand what a name refers to.
- Name a value an update handler constructs before assigning it `next<Field>` (`nextSelectedDate` for `selectedDate`). Threading a destructured payload straight through (`username: () => value`) needs no intermediate.
- Name an update-like result after the operation that produced it: `homeInit`, `dialogClose`. When the operation name collides with the function, use a trailing underscore such as `init_`, not `initialization` or a generic `initResult`. A child fold's `write` parameter is the next child Model, so name it `nextSettings`, `nextDialog`, and so on.

## State Modeling

- Encode state in discriminated unions, not booleans or nullable fields. `Idle | Loading | Error | Ok`, not `isLoading`. Make impossible states unrepresentable.
- Declare all variants together: `defineMessageUnion` for Messages and OutMessages, `defineRouteUnion` for Routes, and `defineTaggedUnion` for other domain unions.
- Use `subset([...])` when a Route or domain Schema accepts only named variants. It includes only the tags named in the call. A variant added to the parent union does not join an existing subset until its tag is added. Do not add `omit`; an exclusion list would silently accept every variant added later.
- Use `taggedStruct` only when the variants cannot be declared together:
  - Recursive unions such as `Canvas.Shape` and the markdown AST.
  - Unions assembled from variants owned by different modules, such as the auth example's `Model`.
  - Tagged child structs that are not union variants, such as `TableRow`.
  - Variants created inside generic Schema factories, such as `AsyncData`.
- If recursion forces one union in a module onto `taggedStruct`, use it for sibling unions in that module too.
- Access each variant through its union: `AppRoute.Person({ personId })` and `FetchState.Ok({ data })`. Do not destructure constructors into sibling bindings. Do not repeat the union name in a tag: `ConnectionState.Connected`, never `ConnectionState.ConnectionConnected`.
- Name a Route union `AppRoute`, not `Route`, which is the Foldkit route module. Use `AppRoute.isAnyOf([...])` instead of writing a `route is A | B` guard by hand.
- Export `type PersonRoute = typeof AppRoute.Person.Type` beside `AppRoute` only when a module needs that variant's type.
- Use `Option` for model fields that represent absence. Not `''` or `0` as the "none" state. Form inputs that start as `''` are actual values, not absent.
- Use `Option` at boundaries where the value will be matched or chained (`Option.match`, `Option.map`, `Option.flatMap`). Simple presence checks don't need it. Don't wrap in `Option` just to check `isSome`.
- When repeated entities can interact concurrently, keep transient interaction state on each entity. Carry the originating identity, such as `pointerId`, in every Message that continues or completes that interaction. Use container-level state only when exclusivity is intentional.
- Errors in Commands become Messages via `Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(ErrorMessage(...)))`. Side effects should never crash the app.
- Fold a Submodel OutMessage by matching on its tag. Always name the variant, even when the union has one variant, in app code, docs, snippets, and examples alike. Never destructure the OutMessage payload without naming the variant.
- Update, init, boot, and component helper producers return `{ model }` when they statically create no Commands. When they compute a Commands collection, return it directly without checking whether it is empty. Never write the literal `commands: []`; `foldkit/no-empty-commands-array` enforces this producer convention.
- Inline `Update.Return<Model, Message>` or `Update.ReturnWithOutMessage<Model, Message, OutMessage>` when a `Message.match` is its only use. Create an `UpdateReturn` alias when another matcher, helper, or exported signature reuses the type. The match generic constrains the whole update, so do not repeat the same return annotation on the function.
- Bind an update-like result to an operation-named value and access its fields through that value. Do not destructure or rename `model`, `commands`, or `outMessage`. Dot access does not prevent someone from ignoring `outMessage`; it keeps the operation and all of its returned fields visible together.
- Pass optional Commands directly to APIs that accept them: `Command.mapMessages(homeInit.commands, toParentMessage)`. Use `result.commands ?? []` only when the next operation requires a concrete array for spreading, concatenating, execution, or an assertion.
- Use `Update.Return<Model, Message>` when an update cannot emit an OutMessage. It prevents a result containing an OutMessage from entering code that would keep only its Model and Commands. A result with no `outMessage` can still be used where `Update.ReturnWithOutMessage<Model, Message, OutMessage>` is expected. The missing field means that update emitted no OutMessage.
- Use `Update.combine` when a later Step should receive the Model produced by an earlier Step. It takes two or more Steps. Do not wrap one Step in `Update.combine`; call that operation directly. Name an inline Step parameter `stepModel`; it contains the Model produced by the preceding Step. Manual unpacking of a child result usually means the site should use `Update.foldChild`, `Update.foldChildAt`, or `Update.foldChildStep` instead. Independent init results may still need separate Model assembly.

# Foldkit

You are working on a Foldkit app. Foldkit is a complete TypeScript frontend framework, built on Effect and architected like Elm. The architecture is solved: state, events, transitions, side effects, streams, routing, UI components, validation, testing, and devtools are all part of the framework, not third-party choices to make. Your job is to model the application's behavior, not to pick libraries or invent architecture.

Foldkit is not incremental. There is no React interop, no escape hatch, no "just do it the React way for this one part." The framework gives you one shape, and there is one way to do most things.

## How to approach the work

- **Pattern-match against Foldkit's own apps.** When the local code doesn't show you the answer (or shows an early-stage version of it), reach into the vendored foldkit subtree. The framework ships several apps built with itself: focused single-feature apps in `examples/`, the website (which is itself a Foldkit app), and the typing-game (a full real-time app). These are the canonical references. Higher fidelity than prose or anything reconstructed from memory.
- **The architecture is not optional.** Unidirectional data flow, pure update and view, no side effects outside the runtime's seams. Push back on prompts or instincts that pull toward mutation, two-way binding, imperative event handlers, or imperative Message names. Propose the idiomatic Foldkit shape and explain why.
- **Foldkit UI is two categories, not one.** Stateful Submodels (Menu, Listbox, Combobox, Calendar, Disclosure, Dialog, Popover, etc.) carry their own Model / Message / update / OutMessage and are embedded via `h.submodel`. Stateless render helpers (Button, Input, Textarea, Select, Fieldset) are called directly with a ViewConfig and the caller's `h`, and return Html. Do not migrate render helpers to Submodels for "consistency": Submodel semantics imply state, and these helpers have none. See the Foldkit UI overview page in the website for the canonical split.
- **Use what the Foldkit and Effect stack provides.** Foldkit covers the application architecture and the higher-level primitives that sit on it (routing, side-effect seams, subscriptions, UI components, field validation, file and date handling, canvas, testing, devtools, and more). Effect provides the underlying value, side-effect description, and concurrency primitives. Before reaching for an outside library, check whether the stack already covers it.
- **Let `modifyFields` setters receive the field.** If a `modifyFields` setter only transforms the current value of that same field, pass the transformer directly (`entries: Array.map(f)`, `count: Number.increment`, `priceSlider: Slider.reflectRange({ min: minPrice, max: maxPrice })`). Use `() => value` for replacement values from Messages, child updates, Commands, or other Model fields.
- **The repo is more authoritative than memory.** When in doubt about a convention, an API, a name, or a pattern, read from the vendored foldkit subtree rather than guessing. Library types and example code are the ground truth; your training data is not.

## Where to look

The foldkit repo is vendored as a git subtree at `repos/foldkit/` from the project root. It is the source of truth for everything: conventions, framework source, examples, the quality bar. Browse it directly.

Stable top-level entry points:

- `repos/foldkit/examples/`: runnable example apps spanning every complexity tier. Usually your first stop when looking for a precedent.
- `repos/foldkit/AGENTS.md`: project conventions and the code-quality bar
- `repos/foldkit/README.md`: framework overview and entry pointers
- `repos/foldkit/skills/`: task-oriented skills with the canonical architecture, conventions, and quality-bar references
- `repos/foldkit/packages/`: framework source and production reference apps (the website, the typing-game, the framework itself)

Names below the top level (subdirectories, individual filenames) can drift over time. List the directory contents to find what you need rather than relying on a path quoted from this skill.

If `repos/foldkit/` is missing from the project, strongly recommend adding it. The subtree is the difference between working from memory and pattern-matching against canonical references. Assistance quality drops noticeably without it. Pin it to the release git tag matching the installed `foldkit` package, so the references describe the APIs the project compiles against rather than whatever `main` holds today. Initialize git first if needed (subtree requires at least one commit):

```
git subtree add --prefix=repos/foldkit https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit.git "foldkit@$(node -p "require('./node_modules/foldkit/package.json').version")" --squash
```

After a Foldkit package upgrade, re-pin with the same command, swapping `add` for `pull`. A canary install (`x.y.z-canary.<commit>` in `node_modules/foldkit/package.json`) has no tag; pin to the full hash of the commit its version names instead, which GitHub expands at `https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/commit/<commit>`.

A consumer project's `FOLDKIT.md` is a scaffolder snapshot and can lag behind the packages it has installed. When it does, replace it whole from `repos/foldkit/packages/create-foldkit-app/templates/base/FOLDKIT.md`. That project's `AGENTS.md` belongs to its author; never overwrite it.

When working inside the foldkit repo itself rather than a consumer project, drop the `repos/foldkit/` prefix. The same paths exist at the project root.

import { Predicate } from 'effect'
import type { Attribute, Html, HtmlBuilder } from 'foldkit/html'

// VIEW

/** Attribute groups the button component provides to the consumer's `toView` callback. */
export type ButtonAttributes<Message> = Readonly<{
  button: ReadonlyArray<Attribute<Message>>
}>

/** Configuration for rendering a button with `view`. */
export type ViewConfig<Message> = Readonly<{
  toView: (attributes: ButtonAttributes<Message>) => Html
  onClick?: Message
  isDisabled?: boolean
  type?: 'button' | 'submit' | 'reset'
  isAutofocus?: boolean
}>

/**
 * Renders an accessible button by building attribute groups and delegating
 * layout to the consumer's `toView` callback.
 *
 * Takes the consumer's builder, which pins `Message` to the universe of the
 * frame the button is rendered in. `onClick` must come from that same
 * universe, so a Message the consumer's dispatcher cannot route is a compile
 * error here.
 */
export const view = <Message>(
  config: ViewConfig<Message>,
  h: HtmlBuilder<Message>,
): Html => {
  const {
    toView,
    onClick,
    isDisabled = false,
    type = 'button',
    isAutofocus = false,
  } = config

  const disabledAttributes = isDisabled
    ? [h.AriaDisabled(true), h.DataAttribute('disabled', '')]
    : []

  const clickAttributes =
    Predicate.isNotUndefined(onClick) && !isDisabled ? [h.OnClick(onClick)] : []

  const autofocusAttributes = isAutofocus ? [h.Autofocus(true)] : []

  const buttonAttributes = [
    h.Type(type),
    h.Tabindex(0),
    ...disabledAttributes,
    ...clickAttributes,
    ...autofocusAttributes,
  ]

  return toView({
    button: buttonAttributes,
  })
}

import { Match, Option } from 'effect'
import type { Attribute, Html, HtmlBuilder } from 'foldkit/html'


export type CheckboxAttributes<Message> = Readonly<{
  checkbox: ReadonlyArray<Attribute<Message>>
  label: ReadonlyArray<Attribute<Message>>
  description: ReadonlyArray<Attribute<Message>>
  hiddenInput: ReadonlyArray<Attribute<Message>>
}>

export type ViewConfig<Message> = Readonly<{
  id: string
  isChecked: boolean
  onToggle: (isChecked: boolean) => Message
  toView: (attributes: CheckboxAttributes<Message>) => Html
  isDisabled?: boolean
  isReadOnly?: boolean
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  hasDescription?: boolean
  name?: string
  value?: string
}>

export const labelId = (id: string): string => `${id}-label`

export const descriptionId = (id: string): string => `${id}-description`

export const view = <Message>(
  config: ViewConfig<Message>,
  h: HtmlBuilder<Message>,
): Html => {
  const {
    id,
    isChecked,
    onToggle,
    toView,
    isDisabled = false,
    isReadOnly = false,
    isIndeterminate = false,
    hasDescription = false,
    name,
    value: formValue = 'on',
  } = config

  const nextChecked = !isChecked

  const handleKeyUp = (key: string): Option.Option<Message> =>
    Match.value(key).pipe(
      Match.when(' ', () => Option.some(onToggle(nextChecked))),
      Match.orElse(() => Option.none()),
    )

  const resolveStateAttributes = () => {
    if (isIndeterminate) {
      return [h.DataAttribute('indeterminate', '')]
    } else if (isChecked) {
      return [h.DataAttribute('checked', '')]
    } else {
      return []
    }
  }

  const disabledAttributes = isDisabled
    ? [h.AriaDisabled(true), h.DataAttribute('disabled', '')]
    : []

  const readOnlyAttributes = isReadOnly
    ? [h.AriaReadonly(true), h.DataAttribute('readonly', '')]
    : []

  const isInteractive = !isDisabled && !isReadOnly

  const describedByAttributes = hasDescription
    ? [h.AriaDescribedBy(descriptionId(id))]
    : []

  const checkboxAttributes = [
    h.Type('button'),
    h.Role('checkbox'),
    h.AriaChecked(isIndeterminate ? 'mixed' : isChecked),
    h.AriaLabelledBy(labelId(id)),
    ...describedByAttributes,
    h.Tabindex(0),
    ...resolveStateAttributes(),
    ...disabledAttributes,
    ...readOnlyAttributes,
    ...(isInteractive
      ? [h.OnClick(onToggle(nextChecked)), h.OnKeyUpPreventDefault(handleKeyUp)]
      : []),
  ]

  const labelAttributes = [
    h.Id(labelId(id)),
    ...(isInteractive ? [h.OnClick(onToggle(nextChecked))] : []),
  ]

  const descriptionAttributes = [h.Id(descriptionId(id))]

  const hiddenInputAttributes = name
    ? [h.Type('hidden'), h.Name(name), h.Value(isChecked ? formValue : '')]
    : []

  return toView({
    checkbox: checkboxAttributes,
    label: labelAttributes,
    description: descriptionAttributes,
    hiddenInput: hiddenInputAttributes,
  })
}

- `pnpm measure` builds every variant twice (with and without Schema) with Vite 8, serves `dist/` from `server.mjs` (gzip level 9, `Cache-Control: no-store`), and measures at mock delay 150 ms.

- The Playwright numbers are optimistic. Evidence: in A, LCP minus FCP is about 500 ms (one modeled RTT of 150 ms, 150 ms server delay, plus transfer), so the question text is correctly placed after the exchange. It is still a model; it was not validated against a real network.
- Playwright cross-check: fresh context per run, 360x740 @2x mobile UA, CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` (150 ms, 1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up) and `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 4, 5 runs. The mock delay is real here. The round trip is the in-page time between marks around `fetch('/answer')`; click to next screen is the click event to the painted screen 2 (rAF + task).

## Caveats

- Lighthouse reports TTI equal to LCP here (no long tasks), and "FMP" no longer exists in Lighthouse 13, so FCP and LCP are the proxies. LCP is the question text arriving from `/exchange`, so LCP is the closest thing to meaningful paint.
- The Playwright numbers are optimistic. The measured POST round trip is about 175-185 ms, barely above the 150 ms mock delay, so the CDP latency emulation clearly did not add a full 150 ms RTT to the in-page requests (it did slow a 75 KB file load when tested in isolation). Treat the Playwright table as a relative comparison and a lower bound; a realistic save round trip is that value plus about one RTT, about 330 ms. Trust Lighthouse for absolute numbers.
- The host has 2 cores and a Lighthouse BenchmarkIndex of about 1340, so 4x throttling is probably a little optimistic for a real mid-range phone. Runs are low-variance but N=5 on one machine says nothing about p75 over real devices.
- Real hosting would serve Brotli (smaller than gzip) over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 with TLS; this server is plain HTTP/1.1 on loopback (TLS adds a round trip the model counts but we did not exercise).
- Base UI's Radio renders a `role=radio` button plus a visually hidden `input type=radio`, not a bare native input as in A, B and C. Accessibility was designed in (fieldset/legend, 44 px targets, visible focus, focus moved to the new screen heading) but not audited with a screen reader or axe.
- Token handling: the page removes the fragment with `history.replaceState` before the POST; the switcher bar (prototype only) is not injected when `bar=0`, so it is not in any measurement.

import { Effect, Option, Schema } from "effect"
import { Command, type Update } from "foldkit"
import type { Document, Html, HtmlBuilder } from "foldkit/html"
import { defineMessageUnion } from "foldkit/message"
import { exchange, markPaint, readFragment, saveAnswer } from "../shared/api"
import { messages, t } from "../shared/messages"
import { Exchange } from "../shared/schema"

export const Model = Schema.Struct({
  token: Schema.String,
  value: Schema.Number,
  exchange: Schema.Option(Exchange),
  screen: Schema.Literals(["q1", "q2"]),
  isFailed: Schema.Boolean,
})
export type Model = typeof Model.Type

export const Message = defineMessageUnion({
  CompletedReadFragment: { token: Schema.String, value: Schema.Number },
  SucceededExchange: { exchange: Exchange },
  FailedExchange: {},
  PickedValue: { value: Schema.Number },
  SubmittedAnswer: {},
  SucceededSaveAnswer: {},
  FailedSaveAnswer: {},
  CompletedMark: {},
})
export type Message = typeof Message.Type

const ReadFragment = Command.define("ReadFragment", {
  messages: [Message.CompletedReadFragment],
  execute: Effect.sync(() => {
    const { token, v } = readFragment()
    return Message.CompletedReadFragment({ token, value: v })
  }),
})
const ExchangeToken = REDACTED, {
  args: { token: Schema.String },
  messages: [Message.SucceededExchange, Message.FailedExchange],
  execute: ({ token }) =>
    Effect.tryPromise(() => exchange(token)).pipe(
      Effect.match({ onSuccess: (exchange) => Message.SucceededExchange({ exchange }), onFailure: () => Message.FailedExchange() }),
    ),
})
const SaveAnswer = Command.define("SaveAnswer", {
  args: { token: Schema.String, questionId: Schema.String, value: Schema.Number },
  messages: [Message.SucceededSaveAnswer, Message.FailedSaveAnswer],
  execute: ({ token, questionId, value }) =>
    Effect.tryPromise(() => saveAnswer(token, questionId, { value })).pipe(
      Effect.match({ onSuccess: () => Message.SucceededSaveAnswer(), onFailure: () => Message.FailedSaveAnswer() }),
    ),
})
const Mark = Command.define("Mark", {
  args: { name: Schema.String },
  messages: [Message.CompletedMark],
  execute: ({ name }) => Effect.sync(() => (markPaint(name), Message.CompletedMark())),
})

export const init = () => ({
  model: { token: "", value: 3, exchange: Option.none(), screen: "q1" as const, isFailed: false },
  commands: [ReadFragment()],
})

export const update = (model: Model, message: Message) =>
  Message.match<Update.Return<Model, Message>>(message, {
    CompletedReadFragment: ({ token, value }) => ({ model: { ...model, token, value }, commands: [ExchangeToken({ token })] }),
    SucceededExchange: ({ exchange }) => ({ model: { ...model, exchange: Option.some(exchange) }, commands: [Mark({ name: "meaningful" })] }),
    FailedExchange: () => ({ model: { ...model, isFailed: true } }),
    PickedValue: ({ value }) => ({ model: { ...model, value } }),
    SubmittedAnswer: () =>
      Option.match(model.exchange, {
        onNone: () => ({ model }),
        onSome: (exchange) => ({ model, commands: [SaveAnswer({ token: model.token, questionId: exchange.questions[0]!.id, value: model.value })] }),
      }),
    SucceededSaveAnswer: () => ({ model: { ...model, screen: "q2" }, commands: [Mark({ name: "screen2" })] }),
    FailedSaveAnswer: () => ({ model: { ...model, isFailed: true } }),
    CompletedMark: () => ({ model }),
  })

const scale = (name: string, value: number, h: HtmlBuilder<Message>): Html =>
  h.div(
    [h.Class("scale")],
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((i) =>
      h.label([], [
        h.input([h.Type("radio"), h.Name(name), h.Value(String(i)), h.Checked(i === value), h.OnChange(() => Message.PickedValue({ value: i }))]),
        messages[`scale.${i}` as "scale.1"],
      ]),
    ),
  )

export const view = (model: Model, h: HtmlBuilder<Message>): Document => {
  const data = Option.getOrUndefined(model.exchange)
  return {
    title: "Answer",
    body: h.main([], [
      h.h1([h.Id("pulse")], [data?.pulseName ?? ""]),
      h.p([h.Class("err"), h.Id("err"), h.Role("alert")], [model.isFailed ? t("error") : ""]),
      model.screen === "q1"
        ? h.section([], [
            h.form([h.Id("f1"), h.OnSubmit(Message.SubmittedAnswer())], [
              h.fieldset([], [h.legend([h.Id("q1text")], [data?.questions[0]?.text ?? t("loading")]), scale("q1", model.value, h)]),
              h.p([h.Class("anon"), h.Id("anon")], [data?.anonymity ?? ""]),
              h.button([h.Type("submit"), h.Id("save"), h.Disabled(data === undefined)], [t("save")]),
            ]),
          ])
        : h.section([], [h.fieldset([], [h.legend([h.Id("q2text")], [data?.questions[1]?.text ?? ""]), scale("q2", 3, h)])]),
    ]),
  }
}

- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` afterwards (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>` (database id, as in **Blocking** below). Without sub-issues, put `Part of #<parent>` at the top of the child body.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh issue create --blocked-by <n>,<n> ...` or `gh issue edit <child> --add-blocked-by <blocker>` (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Count open blockers**: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only; 0 means startable). `gh issue view <n> --json blockedBy` also lists closed blockers, so filter it: `--jq '[.blockedBy.nodes[] | select(.state == "OPEN")] | length'`.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: post the explanation with `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`, then `gh issue close <number>`. On an already-closed issue, `gh issue close --comment` drops the comment and still exits 0.

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

File issues only into the user's own repo. Never file into `mattpocock/skills` (the repo these skills come from) unless the user owns it. In a fork, `gh` can default to the upstream parent, so before the first `gh issue create` of a session, check the target with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` and confirm it with the user if it is not their repo.

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:
